What has happened is that a prodigal political class took over, deliberately ran down the refineries, refused to build new ones and, most criminally, insisted on denominating fuel in inflated dollar accounting. Their paper accounting is based on our country having no drop of oil, which we all know is false, and having to import finished products which are bought by dubious officials from their chosen partners, pay freight, insurance, port fees, demurrage and storage fees. These products are then handed over to a cartel which transports them through deliberately neglected or abandoned roads and sells them to hapless Nigerians at rates imposed by the cartel. In this dubious process is built what is touted as subsidy. Since the Babangida regime, this dubious subsidy mirage has been factored into our petroleum products. When the latest subsidy removal was touted on May 29, 2023, Nigerians were told the proceeds would be used for development. But what we have experienced is greater misery, multiplication of the hungry, dilapidating infrastructure, a rising number of out-of-school children, lack of mass housing, virtually abandoned basic healthcare and insecurity. Whenever we ask the administration what has been done with the so-called subsidy savings, it points at increasing the revenue allocation to states and local governments. It is aware that most leaders of these tiers are like cats being told to watch over fried fish. Deceptively, it does not point at itself as being the largest recipient of these extra funds, which remain unaccounted for. When President Tinubu announced that his administration had removed fuel subsidy, the price of a litre of PMS was increased from about N197 to an average N500. Today, it is thrice that price, and the government blames this insanity on the war in Iran. In this, the Tinubu government is behaving like the dirty widow with head lice creeping all over her hair who blames this on mourning her husband by not allowing a drop of water to touch her head since his demise. If the Nigerian government blames the war in Iran for the outrageous price of PMS in the country, why is Iran, which has suffered the catastrophe of having its leadership wiped out, children buried under the rubble of their classrooms, infrastructure and oil facilities bombed and punishing sanctions imposed by the United States, not been similarly affected? Honourable Victor Afam Oghene, Member, Federal House of Representatives, Ogbaru Constituency of Anambra State, debunked, with verifiable statistics, these childish fairy tales of the Tinubu government. He gave comparative statistics of PMS prices in four oil-producing countries: Iran, which has been at war for years; Libya, which has suffered state collapse since 2011 and had at least three factional governments in Tobruk, Tripoli and Benghazi; Saudi Arabia, which is engaged in war with neighbouring Yemen; and Nigeria, which is not at war. In his statistics, which the increasingly intolerant Tinubu government and its army of internet propagandists have not been able to fault, Honourable Oghene revealed that a litre of PMS in Iran is N38, Libya, N32, Saudi Arabia, N832, and Nigeria, at least N1,300. In contrast, the National Minimum Wage in Iran is N165,000, Libya is N210,000, Saudi Arabia, N1.4 million, and N70,000 in Nigeria! Oghene then analysed these basic statistics in value terms. He showed that the minimum wage in Iran can purchase 4,242 litres of PMS, Libya, 6,562 litres, Saudi Arabia, 1,700, and only 46 litres in Nigeria! Tragically, despite such sound analysis and the situation in the country, the Tinubu administration appears increasingly irritated, deaf to the cries of Nigerians and incapable of basic thinking. For instance, rather than examine the arguments of various patriots and pro-people activists on the issue of fuel subsidy and the calamitous effects on the populace, it is threatening Nigerians with dire consequences. In its unfathomable scare-mongering, the administration’s Minister of Finance, Taiwo Oyedele, threatened that even an inkling of the administration rethinking the subsidy issue would trigger capital flight. This, he claimed, would lead to the naira, which has already been devalued over fifty per cent by Tinubu, suffering a further sixty per cent devaluation. Oyedele told Nigerians this fable, not based on any analysis, but beliefs. He also claimed that this would raise the price of petrol to at least N2,000 per litre. Even as a product of Yale University and London School of Economics, and an advertised policy expert, the Honourable Minister could not provide the cost component of this his projected N2,000-per-litre PMS. We Nigerians never left our Egypt, so there is no issue of a return. It is the prodigals of the political class that need to return home, ask for forgiveness and stop suffocating the country. Under the theme, “Exploring New Horizons with Innovative Solutions,” the conference brought together energy professionals to examine the technologies, engineering practices and operational strategies shaping the industry’s future. For Nigeria, where increasing production, developing natural gas resources and strengthening indigenous operators remain national priorities, the message was clear: innovation must translate into measurable business performance. The global energy industry is under pressure to deliver reliable supplies, improve capital efficiency and reduce environmental impacts. For Africa, these demands coincide with a pressing need to expand electricity access, industrialise economies and create productive employment. The challenge is not simply to defend the relevance of hydrocarbons, but to demonstrate that African energy resources can be developed competitively, responsibly and profitably. The lessons from Houston offer a practical starting point. Artificial intelligence, advanced reservoir analytics, predictive maintenance, drilling automation and digital production monitoring are creating opportunities to improve oil recovery, reduce equipment failures, shorten operational delays and strengthen investment decisions. Their significance lies not in technological novelty, but in their potential to improve the economics of producing assets. Consider Nigeria’s mature oilfields, many of which face declining production, ageing infrastructure, rising water cuts and expensive maintenance requirements. Better integration of geological data, well-performance records and production information can help operators identify underperforming wells, prioritise interventions and determine where additional investment is most likely to recover lost production. Predictive maintenance can similarly help operators identify early warning signs in pumps, compressors and other critical equipment before failures cause costly shutdowns. Improved drilling analytics can support better well planning, reduce non-productive time and strengthen operational safety. Meanwhile, methane monitoring and flare-management technologies can help operators identify emissions sources, reduce avoidable losses and improve environmental performance. These are practical applications for Nigeria’s oil and gas industry, not automatic outcomes of technology adoption. Results depend on reliable data, competent personnel, appropriate infrastructure and disciplined implementation. Every investment should therefore be assessed against measurable indicators, including incremental production, reduced downtime, lower operating costs, improved recovery and emissions reduction. This approach is particularly important as Nigeria’s upstream industry undergoes structural change. The transfer of selected onshore and shallow-water assets from international oil companies to indigenous operators has created opportunities for domestic companies to expand their participation and retain more value within the economy. Yet a change of ownership does not automatically produce higher output, stronger profitability or sustainable operations. Indigenous operators must combine ownership with the technical and financial capacity to manage complex reservoirs, rehabilitate infrastructure, improve recovery and meet environmental obligations. Access to technology, long-term financing, specialised engineering expertise and dependable evacuation systems will be critical to their success. Nigeria’s ambition to achieve three million barrels of crude oil production per day by 2030 must therefore be treated as an execution challenge rather than a statement of intent. New developments, improved recovery from existing fields, reduced production losses, reliable evacuation and sustained investment must work together to deliver the desired outcome. The leadership transition within the SPE Nigeria Council, from Engr. Francis Nwaochei to Engr. Etta Agbor, also presents an opportunity to strengthen the connection between global technical knowledge and local operating realities. Professional institutions such as SPE can support this process through applied research, technical training, industry collaboration and the development of Nigerian engineering talent capable of evaluating and deploying advanced technologies. However, technology alone cannot overcome an uncertain investment environment. Regulatory predictability remains fundamental. The Petroleum Industry Act provides an important statutory framework, but investors also require transparent fiscal arrangements, timely approvals, consistent regulatory decisions and clarity over contractual obligations. Effective regulation should protect public interests while enabling commercially viable projects to proceed without avoidable administrative delays. Security and infrastructure are equally important. Production cannot generate its full economic value if crude oil and gas cannot reach markets reliably. Pipeline disruptions, theft, infrastructure failures and insecurity increase operating costs, undermine revenues and weaken investor confidence. Government institutions, regulators, operators, security agencies and host communities must work together to protect infrastructure and strengthen the reliability of Nigeria’s energy supply chain. Environmental performance is also becoming integral to commercial competitiveness. Methane detection, flare reduction, emissions monitoring and environmental remediation increasingly influence investor assessments and access to international financing. Operators must incorporate these responsibilities into field-development plans and operating budgets rather than treating them as separate sustainability commitments. Beyond upstream production, Africa’s energy investment proposition extends across the value chain. Gas processing, pipelines, gas-to-power, domestic LNG and LPG distribution can support industrial growth where viable markets and bankable offtake arrangements exist. Refining and petrochemical development can create additional value through domestic processing, fertiliser production, manufacturing and associated logistics. Each opportunity, however, requires commercially realistic assumptions, dependable infrastructure and appropriate risk allocation. For international investors, the question is no longer simply whether Africa possesses substantial hydrocarbon resources. It is whether specific projects can offer credible returns, transparent governance, manageable risks and reliable access to markets. African governments and operators must make that case through predictable policies, technical competence and consistent delivery. Industry platforms such as the Nigeria International Energy Summit can help connect technology providers, indigenous operators, regulators, policymakers and international financiers. Their value should ultimately be measured by what follows the discussions: capital mobilised, partnerships established, technology deployed, infrastructure completed and production improved. The message from Houston to Abuja is unmistakable. Africa’s energy future will not be secured by resource abundance alone. It will depend on the disciplined convergence of engineering excellence, investment, reliable infrastructure, environmental responsibility and decisive policy execution. item.title: Okonjo-Iweala loses mother, as Tinubu mourns
item.description: ‎By Johnbosco Agbakwuru PRESIDENT Bola Tinubu has extended his heartfelt condolences to the Okonjo royal family of Ogwashi-Uku, Delta State, on the passing of Prof. Kamene Okonjo, who died at the age of 96. Prof. Okonjo was a distinguished scholar, a champion of women’s empowerment, and a revered matriarch. The President particularly commiserated with her daughter, Dr Ngozi Okonjo-Iweala, Director-General of the World Trade Organisation, other family members, and the people of Ogwashi-Uku over the loss of their beloved mother, matriarch, and community leader. President Tinubu described Prof. Okonjo’s passing as the loss of an accomplished academic whose life was defined by intellectual distinction, service to humanity, and an enduring commitment to advancing women and society. He acknowledged her contributions to scholarship and her inspiring example as a woman who combined professional excellence with dedication to family, community, and the preservation of traditional institutions. The President prayed that Almighty God will grant the departed eternal rest and comfort the family and all who mourn her passing. Vanguard reports that Kamene Okonjo, a professor of sociology and advocate for women’s rights, died on Friday, according to reports citing a statement issued by the Umu Obi Obahai royal family of Ogwashi-Uku kingdom in Delta state. item.title: Soldiers earn peanuts, APC youth leader flaunts billion-naira SUVs — Utomi
item.description: Professor Pat Utomi has criticised the All Progressives Congress (APC) over the distribution of luxury sport utility vehicles (SUVs) to selected youth leaders, contrasting the expenditure with what he described as poor salaries paid to Nigerian soldiers. Utomi, a chieftain of the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC), said it was troubling that an APC youth leader could display expensive vehicles at a time Nigerians had been told that government funds were limited. In a post on X on Sunday, Utomi wrote: “Nigerian soldiers are being paid peanuts as salaries, yet an APC youth leader is flaunting SUVs worth billions of naira. This is the same government that told Nigerians there was no longer money in the treasury. At this point, they must think we are fools!” In another post, the professor questioned whether the money spent on the vehicles could have been put to better use, particularly in the health sector. “Each of the SUVs in this video costs more than ₦100 million. I wonder how many world-class ambulances the millions being spent on these vehicles could buy. What a pity!” he wrote. The comments followed a video posted by APC National Youth Leader, Dayo Israel, showing brand-new 2026 Toyota Prado SUVs he said were presented to selected youth leaders to support election mobilisation ahead of the 2027 general elections. “Today, I presented brand new 2026 Prado to my committed selected youth leaders to aid their election mobilisation activities,” Israel wrote. He also expressed gratitude to First Lady Oluremi Tinubu for what he described as her continued support for the party’s structure under his leadership. “The party is supreme and that supremacy will show in our action in this election period — we will deliver polling unit by polling unit,” he added. The video, which has since been deleted, drew criticism from Nigerians on social media, with some questioning the timing of the vehicle distribution amid the economic hardship associated with the Tinubu administration’s reforms. Utomi’s remarks add to the criticism surrounding the display, with the NDC chieftain raising questions about public spending priorities and the cost of the vehicles. item.description: Kylian Mbappe struck twice to earn Jose Mourinho’s Real Madrid a 2-1 Clasico victory over La Liga leaders Barcelona on Sunday at Camp Nou, cutting the gap to three points. Real Madrid remain third, behind Atletico Madrid and Hansi Flick’s Barca, who had won their first nine games before a chastening week. The Catalans suffered a second straight defeat after losing on Tuesday against Paris Saint-Germain in the Champions League. Barca had won six of the seven previous Clasicos since the German arrived but were surprisingly subdued against Mourinho’s side. Los Blancos, without suspended winger Vinicius Junior, won their fifth straight game across all competitions and are finding their footing under veteran Portuguese coach Mourinho. The opening period of the game was cagey, with few opportunities. Barca defender Pau Cubarsi twice reacted well to shut down Mbappe, while Real Madrid’s Marc Cucurella took a rapid liking for Lamine Yamal’s shirt, constantly grabbing at the 19-year-old winger. Anthony Gordon, playing in his first Clasico since joining Barcelona from Newcastle, backheeled the ball to Raphinha, who fired narrowly wide as Barca threatened. item.title: U-17 Women’s World Cup: 3 African countries qualify for Round of 16 [Full list]
item.description: Three African countries, Nigeria, Ghana and Morocco, have qualified for the Round of 16 at the 2026 FIFA U-17 Women’s World Cup in Morocco. The trio are among 16 teams that have advanced to the knockout stage of the competition, which features some of the best young women’s football teams from around the world. item.title: ‘Filled with content creators’ — Bwala disparages NDC campaign council list
item.description: Daniel Bwala, an aide to President Bola Tinubu, has criticised the Nigeria Democratic Congress (NDC) over its National Campaign Council for the 2027 general elections, describing the list as being “filled with content creators”. Bwala, in a post on X shortly after the party announced the council on Sunday, also accused the NDC of concealing the identities of its media surrogates in mainstream media. “@PeterObi and NDC have released their list of campaign council members; and as expected it is filled with content creators,” he wrote. “They stylishly refused to name their campaign media surrogates in the mainstream media masquerading as OAP.” @PeterObi and NDC have released their list of campaign council members; and as expected it is filled with content creators. They stylishly refused to name their campaign media surrogates in the mainstream media masquerading as OAP. — D. H Bwala (@BwalaDaniel) October 25, 2026 The NDC had earlier announced the constitution of its National Campaign Council, saying it would coordinate campaign activities nationwide and mobilise support for its candidates ahead of the 2027 elections. Under the arrangement, the party’s National Leader, Senator Henry Seriake Dickson, will serve as chairman, while its presidential candidate, Peter Obi, will be co-chairman. The party’s National Chairman, Senator Cleopas Moses Zuwoghe, was named vice-chairman, while its vice-presidential candidate, Senator Rabiu Musa Kwankwaso, will serve as co-vice-chairman. The NDC’s National Secretary, Barrister Ikenna Morgan Enekweizu, was named council secretary, while Mallam Ibrahim Hussain Abdulkarim will serve as director-general. Announcing the council, the party said it would provide “strategic leadership” and drive nationwide mobilisation behind its vision of “a new, just, and prosperous Nigeria”. The NDC also said the council would deliver a “people-centred and issue-based campaign” and urged its members, supporters and other Nigerians to remain united ahead of the elections. Bwala’s comments came shortly after the announcement, as political parties prepare their structures and mobilisation strategies for the 2027 general elections. item.title: Opebi-Mende-Ojota Link Bridge To Be Opened Before Christmas, Says Sanwo-Olu
item.description: The Lagos State Governor Babajide Sanwo-Olu has said that the Opebi-Mende Link Bridge is about 80 per cent complete, expressing confidence that the project will be opened to the public before Christmas. Governor Sanwo-Olu gave the assurance during an inspection of the project, acknowledging that the construction had exceeded the September completion timeline previously announced. He said his visit to the site was to establish the reasons for the delay and assess the progress of work, stressing that the project’s distinctive architectural design and engineering requirements must not be compromised by the pressure to meet the deadline. He explained that the bridge’s steel structure was designed to reflect the area’s historical association with cane weaving, thereby preserving its cultural identity. According to him, the project involves installing more than 300 tonnes of steel at heights of up to 25 metres, making it an unusually demanding engineering undertaking. The governor said three of the four major steel components, designed to resemble interwoven cane, had been completed, while work was ongoing on the remaining component. He added that light-emitting diode (LED) installations featuring the colours of Lagos State would enhance the structure and give it an iconic appearance. Governor Sanwo-Olu added that the state government would not sacrifice engineering quality and public safety for speed, despite the delay. He said additional activities, including site cleaning, repainting of kerbs, restoration of affected areas and landscaping, would be undertaken before the bridge is opened to the public. He envisaged the area becoming a destination for recreation, cultural heritage and tourism, adding that its redevelopment would enable residents to appreciate the history and identity of the community. The governor maintained that the bridge would become a significant infrastructure landmark in Lagos, combining innovation with cultural preservation. Sanwo-Olu commissioned the construction of the bridge in 2022 to ease congestion in Ikeja and environs. Governor Sanwo-Olu (centre) He said that the bridge, which is part of the ‘legacy project,’ was an innovative solution to the perennial gridlock around Opebi/Mobolaji Bank Anthony Way/Ojota/Mende corridor. item.title: Bayern beat Freiburg to reclaim top spot as Kompany remains hospitalised
item.description: Bayern Munich reclaimed top spot in the Bundesliga with a 3-1 win at Freiburg on Sunday, days after coach Vincent Kompany was hospitalised when he collapsed at training. Bayern were missing several first-team players and Kompany, but cruised to a two-goal lead at half-time with Dayot Upamecano and Serge Gnabry scoring. Freiburg pulled one back and were pushing for a point in stoppage time when goalkeeper Mio Backhaus was caught out up the field, allowing Michael Olise to slide the ball into an empty net. Kompany remains in hospital and is being treated for a mystery virus, with Bayern saying Saturday the coach is likely to be out for “days, not weeks”. “I just opened my phone to a message from Vince saying ‘well done’ and he was happy,” assistant coach Aaron Danks told DAZN. “I just replied saying ‘brilliant — now go rest’. I sent him a kissing emoji, so hopefully he rests up.” Bayern sporting director Max Eberl gave an update on Kompany’s condition. “He’s stable. He no longer has a headache. He’s now undergoing a thorough examination. Everything is being handled,” he said. “There’s no diagnosis, nothing final yet.” With victory Bayern leapfrogged Borussia Dortmund to top the table ahead of the duo’s clash in Munich next week. Harry Kane had a close-range effort saved late in the second half but failed to find the net a day before the Ballon d’Or ceremony in London, with the England captain among the favourites. Bayern arrived in the Black Forest after a tumultuous few days which left them lacking leaders. With coach Kompany still in hospital after collapsing on Friday, Englishman Danks was in the dugout. The visitors were also without injured captain Manuel Neuer, Luis Diaz, Jamal Musiala, Aleksandar Pavlovic and Kim Min-jae, while midfielder and Germany captain Joshua Kimmich was on bereavement leave due to the sudden death of his father. Bayern were in the unusual position of sitting back and absorbing pressure as Freiburg pushed, but took the lead after 16 minutes when Upamecano started and finished a length-of-the-field counter. The France defender won possession near his own box, played a one-two with Olise before thundering goalwards and sending a cool shot past Backhaus. Bayern doubled up just before the break when Gnabry latched onto a Nathaniel Brown pass and nutmegged Backhaus to score. With 10 minutes remaining, Kane stung Backhaus’s palms from close range and the hosts went on an immediate counter, forcing Tom Bischof into conceding an own goal. The goal sparked Freiburg to life and Bayern ‘keeper Jonas Urbig needed to make crucial saves from Igor Matanovic in the dying moments. item.description: The recent voter registration figures released by the Independent National Electoral Commission (INEC) have raised important questions about the declining number of young people on Nigeria’s voter register. item.title: 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations
item.description: By Dickson Omobola President Bola Tinubu has appointed Minister of Aviation and Aerospace Development, Festus Keyamo, to head the Directorate of Air Mobilisation of the All Progressives Congress, APC, 2027 re-election campaign Keyamo would serve as Director of the Directorate of Air Mobilisation, with the Managing Director of the Federal Airports Authority of Nigeria, FAAN, Mrs Olubunmi Kuku, appointed Deputy Director 1, while Engr Farouk Ahmed Umar would serve as Deputy Director II. Special Adviser on Media and Communications to the Minister, Tunde Moshood, in a statement, said the appointments underscored the strategic importance of air transportation, operational coordination and aviation logistics to the organisation of a nationwide presidential campaign in a country as geographically extensive as Nigeria. The statement reads: ‘The Directorate of Air Mobilisation is expected to play a crucial role in coordinating the campaign’s air-movement requirements, facilitating travel arrangements for designated campaign officials and personnel, and ensuring effective planning for air transportation in support of campaign activities across the six geopolitical zones of the country. “Given the scale of the 2027 presidential campaign, the directorate is expected to work closely with other relevant campaign structures to promote seamless coordination, operational efficiency and effective deployment of available logistical resources, subject to applicable aviation regulations and electoral laws. “Keyamo’s appointment brings to the campaign structure the experience of a serving aviation minister who has been at the forefront of policy initiatives aimed at strengthening Nigeria’s aviation sector, improving its international standing and positioning the country as a major aviation hub in Africa. “His familiarity with the operational demands of the aviation industry is expected to provide useful leadership in coordinating the directorate’s activities and establishing an effective framework for air-mobilisation planning. “The appointment of Mrs. Olubunmi Kuku and Umar as Deputy Directors also brings aviation-sector leadership and technical experience into the directorate, strengthening its capacity to address the planning and coordination demands associated with nationwide campaign movements.” The post 2027: Keyamo to lead APC presidential campaign air operations appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Learn leadership from Macron amid killings, hardship – ADC to Tinubu
item.description: By Luminous Jannamike ABUJA – The African Democratic Congress Presidential Campaign Council (ADC-PCC) on Sunday challenged President Bola Tinubu to learn from French President Emmanuel Macron, accusing him of failing to show sufficient empathy for Nigerians grappling with insecurity, hunger and economic hardship. The council said the reported postponement of Macron’s scheduled state visit to Nigeria underscored the need for leaders to pay attention to pressing domestic challenges, arguing that Nigerians facing killings, mass abductions and rising living costs deserve more visible concern from their president. In a statement by its Director of Media and Publicity, Kola Ologbondiyan, the ADC-PCC cited reports that Macron had rescheduled his October 28–29, 2026 visit to Nigeria, including the planned France-Nigeria Business Forum in Lagos, to early 2027 amid domestic challenges in France. “A president will not travel when his home is contending with internal combustion,” a Nigerian official familiar with the development was quoted as saying. The ADC-PCC said the welfare of citizens should remain central to governance, citing attacks and killings in Plateau, Niger, Benue, Zamfara, Kaduna, Kogi, Kwara, Katsina, Sokoto and other parts of the country. It also raised concerns over a reported incident in Niger State involving the detention of more than 60 young Nigerians under allegedly inhumane conditions, with over 37 reportedly dying in custody. Describing the incident as a grave national concern, the council demanded urgent government intervention, accountability and justice for the affected families. It faulted Tinubu’s response, claiming that Vice President Kashim Shettima visited the state weeks after the incident, following a visit by former Vice President Atiku Abubakar to commiserate with affected communities and bereaved families. The council said Atiku’s visit demonstrated the importance of identifying with citizens in moments of grief, arguing that public office holders must show concern through direct engagement with affected people, not merely official statements. “President Macron has offered a reminder that the concerns of citizens must remain central to leadership. When a country faces a serious domestic crisis, its leadership must demonstrate urgency, compassion and a willingness to take responsibility,” the council said. The ADC-PCC urged the Tinubu administration to prioritise the protection of lives, tackle insecurity and ease the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It also demanded answers over deaths in custody and alleged unlawful detention, insisting that affected families deserved justice and those responsible should be held accountable. The ADC-PCC urged the Tinubu administration to prioritise the protection of lives, tackle insecurity and ease the economic hardship confronting Nigerians. It also demanded answers over deaths in custody and alleged unlawful detention, insisting that affected families deserved justice and those responsible should be held accountable. item.title: My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power
item.description: By Ayo Onikoyi Actress Uzoamaka Power, known for her role in The Call of My Life, has revealed that her father’s perception of acting initially made her afraid to pursue her dream of becoming an actress. Speaking during an interview on the Tea With Tay podcast, Power recalled how her father frequently criticised actresses whenever they appeared on television, questioning their dressing and commitment to education. “With my father, I was cowardly about pursuing my dreams because my father’s idea of acting, the way he saw acting, was prostitution,” she said. According to her, watching films with her father often meant listening to his disapproval of the women appearing on screen. “Anytime we watched a film, he was always criticising the women. He would be like, ‘Don’t they have parents? Look at what they are wearing, and they are in the university. When do they have time to study?’” Despite his reservations, Power said she had always been certain about her desire to become an actress and believed she would succeed in the profession. “I had a knowing in me that I was going to be an actor, and I knew I was going to succeed doing this thing I love doing,” she said. The actress, however, acknowledged that her father’s concerns came from a place of care, explaining that he wanted her to pursue a career he considered more financially secure. “I understood that he was looking out for me and he wanted the best for me. He also knew these kinds of jobs were not sustainable. You needed, like, an office job,” she recalled. Speaking further about her personality and how she handles perceptions of arrogance, Power maintained that she had never felt the need to diminish herself to make others comfortable. “I have never felt the need to downplay myself or to make myself feel small for the benefit of everyone else. I have always known who I am. I have always known my shortcomings, to be honest,” she said. She added that being aware of her strengths and limitations had helped her remain comfortable with herself, regardless of how others interpreted her confidence. “I am very honest with myself about where I am, what I am doing, what I am capable of, what I am unable to do, and whether I am willing to learn. “So, I have just been myself, really. And if anyone considers that not being humble, I am sorry, I can’t,” she said. The post My father saw acting as prostitution — Uzoamaka Power appeared first on Vanguard News .

item.title: Police Foil Railway Vandalism, Arrest Four Suspects With 70 Stolen Sleepers In Katsina
item.description: The Katsina State Police Command has arrested four suspected railway vandals and recovered 70 railway sleepers believed to have been stolen. The suspects were apprehended on October 11, 2026, at about 12:30 a.m., when police operatives on routine stop-and-search duty along the Kurfi–Tsanni Village Road intercepted a white J5 vehicle. The vehicle, driven by a 25-year-old man, was said to be carrying three other occupants. A thorough search of the vehicle uncovered 70 railway sleepers carefully concealed behind 17 bags of animal feed in what investigators believe was an attempt to evade detection. Police said preliminary investigations revealed that one of the suspects confessed to receiving the railway materials from a suspected supplier from Bauchi State, who is currently at large. The police said 70 railway sleepers were carefully concealed behind 17 bags of animal feed in what investigators believe was an attempt to evade detection. According to the police command, the stolen items were being transported for delivery to a man in Katsina. It said that the four suspects are currently in police custody, while the operational vehicle, the recovered railway sleepers and the bags of animal feed used to conceal them have been secured as exhibits. The Command said efforts are underway to apprehend the fleeing suspects and determine the exact location from which the railway infrastructure was vandalised, adding that investigations are ongoing. In a statement issued on Sunday, the Police Public Relations Officer, DSP Abubakar Sadiq, described the arrests as another breakthrough in the fight against crimes targeting critical national infrastructure. Sadiq said the Commissioner of Police, CP Ali Umar Fage, reaffirmed the Command’s unwavering commitment to protecting critical national infrastructure and bringing perpetrators of vandalism to justice. The PPRO said that the commissioner also appealed to residents to continue supporting security agencies with timely and credible information that will enable the police to prevent crime and swiftly apprehend criminal elements across the state.
